# Feature: Opt-In Vision Assist

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-036
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_interaction_wave2.md`

Give the agent a **consent-gated, budgeted, fully audited** way to look at the page when text observation is insufficient or contradicts observed behavior — and make it structurally impossible to do so by accident.

A screenshot is the one model-visible payload the sanitizer cannot see into. Every other payload passes `sanitize(payload, profile, hostHint?)`; pixels do not. A capture of a logged-in page carries names, balances, message bodies, and account numbers as raw bytes to the configured model provider, and also leaves them on disk in the run directory. The user value this feature delivers is therefore **two-sided**:

- When the user explicitly opts in, a stuck run gets fallback visual evidence instead of burning turns re-observing a page whose text shape is lying to it.
- When the user has not opted in — which is the default, and the state of every run until the user acts — the capability does not exist. Not refused at call time: **not registered**, so the model is never told it is there and there is no path, prompt-injection or otherwise, to reach it.

Concretely, this feature ships:

1. `context.screenshots` — a new profile/preference grant, **default false**, resolved through the existing `profile.yaml ⊕ index.db` effective view.
2. A loud, specific warning printed **before** the grant is written, naming what is exposed and where it goes, softened but never removed for a local provider.
3. `browser_screenshot` — an agent-requested tool registered only when **five** conditions all hold, and structurally absent otherwise.
4. A set-of-marks overlay that draws Yantra's own `eNN` refs (and nothing else) onto Yantra's own capture, with mandatory removal.
5. A fail-closed `SensitiveScreenLatch` that refuses capture from the moment a resolved secret could be on screen until the document epoch actually changes.
6. Hard binary budgets (≤3 captures/run, ≤1600×1200 px, PNG only, ≤5 MiB encoded per capture) charged to **dedicated** counters, failing closed.
7. Full audit: captures written to `runs/<id>/screenshots/`, referenced as metadata (never pixels) from `tool-calls.jsonl`, surfaced by `yantra audit`, with the raw Pi session log honestly labeled capture-bearing.

**Non-goal, stated up front:** vision must never become load-bearing. The full 17-fixture gauntlet passes with vision disabled, and this feature adds no gauntlet fixture that requires sight (plan §9).

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does **not** exist, and plan §4 is explicit that **no new relational schema and no Data Modeller pass is needed**. The vision grant is **one additional JSON value in the existing keyed `preferences` table / effective profile view — no new table and no migration**, because the preferences table already stores keyed JSON (`key TEXT`, JSON `value`, `source`, `approved`) and the effective view merges the `profile.yaml` layer over it. Adding `context.screenshots` is a schema-registration change in `KNOWN_PREFERENCE_KEYS` / `profileSchema`, not a DDL change. The other two shapes below are **not relational at all**: `Capture` is a filesystem artifact plus a JSONL metadata record, and `SensitiveScreenLatch` is in-memory run-local state that never persists.

### Entities & Attributes

- **VisionGrant** (durable; existing keyed preferences table + `profile.yaml`, no new table)
  - `key` (string literal `'context.screenshots'`) — new member of `KNOWN_PREFERENCE_KEYS` in `packages/core/src/profile/profile-file.ts`.
  - `value` (boolean) — schema `z.boolean()` in `KEY_VALUE_SCHEMAS`; CLI string coercion accepts only `true` / `false` (same branch as `context.location` / `personalization.enabled`); anything else is rejected by the schema.
  - `source` (`'user' | 'learned'`) — existing column. **A `learned` row can never grant vision**: this key is never machine-written, and resolution requires `approved === true` anyway.
  - `approved` (boolean) — existing column. Unapproved ⇒ denied.
  - `profile.yaml` layer: `context.screenshots` added to the `context` block with **default `false`**, and to `flattenProfile()`.
  - **Resolution rule (the whole security property):** granted **iff** the effective entry exists, is `approved`, is `typeof value === 'boolean'`, and is exactly `true`. Absent, unapproved, unset, non-boolean, or `false` all resolve to **denied**.
  - **Deliberate asymmetry with `context.location`, preserved and tested:** `resolveAmbientGrants` today returns `{ location: approvedBoolean(prefs, 'context.location') !== false }` — location defaults **true** because stating a location the user already configured is behavior-preserving for a fact already being rendered. Screenshots default **false** and must use `=== true`, not `!== false`. The two lines sit next to each other and must not be "unified".

- **ModelVisionCapability** (run-local, resolved once, before tool-catalog construction)
  - `imageInput` (boolean) — whether the **resolved** model declares image input. Derived in the Pi adapter from the SDK's `Model.input: ("text" | "image")[]` (verified in `@earendil-works/pi-ai` `types.d.ts`), i.e. `model.input.includes('image')`.
  - `resolvedAt` (`'pre-catalog'`) — a marker asserted by tests, because the sequencing is the requirement (see TASK-004).
  - Provider-neutral: the boolean crosses into `RunServices`; the Pi `Model` type never does (memory: only `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/` may import the provider SDK).

- **VisionAvailability** (run-local, derived once, immutable for the run) — the five-condition conjunction evaluated before `createYantraTools`:
  - `grantEnabled` (boolean) — the VisionGrant above.
  - `hasBrowserTools` (boolean) — the resolved `CommandTaskProfile.toolNames` contains the browser interaction tools (i.e. `services.domain.browser !== null` and the profile grants browser tools).
  - `modelImageInput` (boolean) — ModelVisionCapability.
  - `suppressedByFlag` (boolean) — `--no-screenshots` present on this invocation.
  - `zeroLlm` (boolean) — scheduled/daemon run or nested `workflow_run` (memory: these are **hard** zero-LLM regardless of flags or environment).
  - `available = grantEnabled && hasBrowserTools && modelImageInput && !suppressedByFlag && !zeroLlm`.

- **Capture** (run state; filesystem artifact + JSONL metadata record — no table)
  - `path` (string) — run-relative, always `screenshots/<seq>-<sha256-prefix>.png`. Stored **relative** so a moved run directory stays auditable (matches the existing movable-run-dir property).
  - `sha256` (string, 64 lowercase hex) — digest of the encoded PNG bytes on disk.
  - `mime_type` (string literal `'image/png'`) — PNG only; anything else is rejected before the file is written.
  - `width`, `height` (integers) — pixel dimensions of the encoded image, ≤ 1600 × 1200.
  - `bytes` (integer) — encoded byte length on disk, ≤ 5 MiB (5 _ 1024 _ 1024).
  - `scope` (`'viewport' | 'element'`) plus `ref` (string, `eNN`, present only when `scope === 'element'`).
  - `marks` (integer) — count of `eNN` labels the overlay drew. Structural only; carries no page text.
  - `seq` (integer, 1-based) — capture ordinal within the run, ≤ 3.
  - **Invariant: no field of `Capture` ever holds image data, base64, or a data URI.** The record is the only thing that reaches `tool-calls.jsonl`, `report.md`, and Pino.

- **CaptureBudget** (run-local counters on `BudgetTracker`, deliberately separate from the text counters)
  - `captureCount` (integer, limit 3) — dedicated; **not** `totalCalls`.
  - `capturePixels` (integer, per-capture limit 1600 \* 1200 = 1,920,000) — dedicated.
  - `captureBytes` (integer, per-capture limit 5 MiB) — dedicated; **not** `cumulativeBytes` / `maxBytesPerResult`. An accepted capture must leave `cumulativeBytes` unchanged except for its own bounded **text** metadata block.
  - All three **fail closed**: an unknown, unmeasurable, or malformed dimension/byte count denies the capture rather than defaulting to allowed.

- **SensitiveScreenLatch** (run-local, in-memory, never persisted, never model-visible)
  - `latched` (boolean) — initially `false`.
  - `latchedAtEpoch` (integer | null) — the `PageSettler` navigation epoch (`packages/core/src/browser/page-settle.ts`, `get epoch()`, bumped on `framenavigated`) observed at latch time.
  - `reason` (`'secret-dispatch'`) — the only reason in this wave.
  - **Set** before a resolved secret is dispatched to the page — i.e. before `withSecret(resolved.value, …)` runs in `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-element.ts`, and specifically before the secret string reaches any port/controller call.
  - **Cleared only** by (a) a top-level document-epoch change (`settler.epoch !== latchedAtEpoch` for the **top-level** document, not a subframe) or (b) browser teardown. Never by a click, a DOM mutation, a dialog dismissal, a guessed submit, a timer, or an SPA route change that does not bump the epoch.
  - **Uncertainty denies.** If the epoch cannot be read, the controller has no page, or the latch state is indeterminate, capture is refused. An SPA that never navigates remains uncapturable for the rest of the run, and that is the intended, documented behavior.

### Relationships

- **VisionGrant** 1:N **Capture** — the grant is _profile_ state, the captures are _run_ state. The grant is necessary but not sufficient: `VisionAvailability` gates registration and `CaptureBudget` + `SensitiveScreenLatch` gate each individual capture.
- **VisionAvailability** 1:1 **run** — computed once, before `createYantraTools`, and never recomputed. It cannot flip mid-run, because the tool catalog (and its hash) is fixed at session open.
- **Capture** 1:1 **tool-call entry** in `tool-calls.jsonl` via `call_id` — each accepted capture contributes exactly one metadata record to its `end` entry.
- **SensitiveScreenLatch** 1:1 **run** (single run-local instance shared by every tool through `RunServices`); it has no relationship to any persisted entity.

### Indexes & Constraints

- No index changes. `preferences` is already keyed by `key`; `context.screenshots` is one more key in that space.
- **No migration.** Confirmed against `packages/core/src/profile/profile-file.ts` (`KNOWN_PREFERENCE_KEYS`, `KEY_VALUE_SCHEMAS`, `flattenProfile`) and the keyed-JSON `preferences` table.
- `runs/<id>/screenshots/` is created lazily on the first accepted capture, with directory mode `0o700` and file mode `0o600` where the OS supports them — matching the existing `runs/<id>/captures/<ref>.txt` precedent for private run artifacts.
- `ToolAuditEntry` (`packages/protocol/src/schemas/tool-audit.ts`) is `.strict()`, so the capture metadata needs an explicitly declared **optional** field (`captures`). Optional keeps every existing run artifact valid — no run directory is rewritten.

## 4. Dependencies

- **Independent of the rest of Wave 2.** FEAT-036 touches the consent, provider-seam, budget, and audit surfaces; FEAT-032/033/034/035/037 touch the interaction/recovery/observation surfaces. There is no ordering constraint between them, and **FEAT-036 must not add a gauntlet fixture that requires sight** — the gauntlet's 17-fixture gate is owned by FEAT-032/033/037 and must pass with vision disabled.
- **Builds on existing, already-implemented infrastructure** (verified in the codebase, not assumed):
  - Preference/profile stack — `KNOWN_PREFERENCE_KEYS` / `profileSchema` / `flattenProfile` / `KEY_VALUE_SCHEMAS` in `packages/core/src/profile/profile-file.ts`; `SqlitePreferenceStore` + `store.effective(yamlLayer)` merge in `apps/cli/src/preferences.ts`; `resolveAmbientGrants` / `resolveUserLocation` in `packages/core/src/profile/ambient-context.ts`; `yantra prefs get|set|list|approve|--forget`.
  - Tool middleware pipeline and `YantraToolResult` in `packages/agent/src/runtime/middleware.ts`, including `sanitizeAndBound()` and `services.budgets.accountResultBytes()`.
  - Tool registration/catalog construction in `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/index.ts` (`buildYantraWrappedTools` → `createYantraTools` / `yantraToolCatalog`, name-sorted for `tool_catalog_hash`).
  - `BudgetTracker` in `packages/agent/src/runtime/budget.ts`.
  - `tool-calls.jsonl` projection: `ToolAuditEntry` (`packages/protocol/src/schemas/tool-audit.ts`) written by `ToolCallWriter` (`packages/core/src/audit/tool-call-writer.ts`) via `RunRecorder`.
  - `yantra audit` (`apps/cli/src/commands/audit.ts` → `buildAuditReport` → `AuditRenderReport` in `apps/cli/src/render/types.ts`).
  - Run-artifact layout under `runs/<id>/` — `manifest.json`, `events.jsonl`, `tool-calls.jsonl`, `trace.json`, `agent/` (raw Pi session), `captures/<ref>.txt` (mode 0600, the private-artifact precedent).
  - Secret execution boundary — `DefaultOpaqueRefResolver` (`packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts`), `deps.secretResolver.resolve(...)` + `withSecret(...)` in `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-element.ts`, and `assertHostBinding`.
  - Navigation epoch — `PageSettler.epoch` in `packages/core/src/browser/page-settle.ts`, bumped on `framenavigated`.
  - `eNN` ref minting — `packages/core/src/browser/agent-controller.ts` (`ref = \`e${this.nextRef++}\``).
- **No new package dependency.** Capture uses `puppeteer-core`'s CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` (already pinned); the overlay is in-DOM precisely to avoid `sharp`/`canvas`. Per memory ("check with the user before pinning a specific new dependency") and plan §3's stated fallback: **if overlay removal cannot be made reliable under navigation races, stop and raise the post-processing dependency question with the user — do not pin `sharp` or `canvas` unilaterally.**
- **New state, not a prerequisite:** `SensitiveScreenLatch` does not exist today and is built here (plan §6).

### TASK-005: Five-condition registration gate — structurally unavailable, not merely refused

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `'browser_screenshot'` to `YantraToolName` in `packages/agent/src/runtime/profiles.ts` (**not** to `ALL_TOOLS` or `BROWSE_TOOLS` — availability, not the profile preset, is what registers it). In `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/index.ts`, `buildYantraWrappedTools` appends `wrapTool(browserScreenshotSpec(toolServices), toolServices)` **only** when `services.vision.available` — the conjunction from TASK-004 of (a) `context.screenshots === true`, (b) the run has browser tools, (c) the resolved model declares image input, (d) `--no-screenshots` absent, (e) the context is not zero-LLM. Zero-LLM (scheduled/daemon runs and nested `workflow_run`, which memory makes **hard** zero-LLM regardless of flags or environment) and image-incapable contexts must produce **no registration at all**, regardless of grant. ### TASK-008: `SensitiveScreenLatch` — set before secret dispatch, cleared only by a top-level document epoch or teardown

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/browser/sensitive-screen-latch.ts` with run-local, in-memory state: `latch(epoch)`, `isLatched(currentTopLevelEpoch)`, `clearOnTeardown()`. `isLatched` returns `true` whenever the latch is set and the **top-level** document epoch still equals `latchedAtEpoch`; it returns `true` (denying capture) whenever the current epoch cannot be determined — **uncertainty denies**. Nothing else clears it: not a click, not a DOM mutation, not a dialog dismissal, not a guessed submit, not a timer, not a subframe navigation, not an SPA route change that does not bump the epoch. Read the epoch from the existing `PageSettler.epoch` (`packages/core/src/browser/page-settle.ts`, bumped on `framenavigated`), filtered to the top-level frame. In `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-element.ts`, call `latch(...)` **before** the resolved secret is dispatched to the page — i.e. before `withSecret(resolved.value, …)` invokes `fillSecretField`, and before any port/controller call can carry secret material. Latch in a `try` that precedes dispatch so an exception during dispatch leaves the latch **set**, never cleared. Clear on `AgentBrowserController.teardown()`. Wire the latch into `RunServices` so `browser_screenshot` consults the same instance, and deny with a stable `SCREENSHOT_SENSITIVE_SCREEN` code while latched.

### TASK-009: Set-of-marks overlay — our refs only, mandatory removal, epoch-guarded

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/browser/set-of-marks.ts`. It injects a single container element that draws **only Yantra's own `eNN` ref labels** at the bounding boxes of currently observed interactables — it must **not** draw page content, page text, values, or anything derived from the page beyond geometry. Contract: (i) `try/finally` with removal in the `finally`, so removal runs on success, on capture error, and on throw; (ii) a **document-epoch guard** — the epoch is read before injection and re-checked before capture and before removal; a change aborts the capture and the artifact is discarded; (iii) **removal verification** — after removal, re-query for the container and fail loudly if it is still present, rather than assuming; (iv) failure cleanup — any injection/capture failure still attempts removal and reports the outcome. This is the one permitted page mutation in this feature and is allowed **only** as a deliberate, audited, agent-requested **capture** stage — never from `detect()`, observation, or any read path (memory: "widget detection must never mutate page state"). Assert that separately (see Unit Tests). **Plan §3 fallback, to be honored rather than worked around:** if removal cannot be made reliable under navigation races, stop and **raise the post-processing dependency question with the user** — do not pin `sharp` or `canvas` unilaterally (memory: check before pinning a new dependency).

### TASK-010: `browser_screenshot` — the capture, the private artifact, and the bounded text result

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-screenshot.ts`. Parameters: optional `ref` (`eNN`) to scope the capture to one element, otherwise the viewport. Flow: check the latch (TASK-008) → `reserveCapture()` (TASK-007) → inject the overlay (TASK-009) → CDP `Page.captureScreenshot` via `puppeteer-core` producing **PNG only**, clipped/bounded to ≤ 1600 × 1200 → remove the overlay → measure encoded bytes and dimensions → `accountCaptureBytes()` → write to `runs/<id>/screenshots/<seq>-<sha256-prefix>.png` with directory mode `0o700` and file mode `0o600` where the OS supports them (matching the existing `runs/<id>/captures/` precedent) → build `CaptureMetadata` → return a bounded, sanitized **text** block (path, sha256, mime, dimensions, bytes, scope, ref, marks count, remaining capture budget) plus **one** image block through the TASK-006 union. Nothing about the page's textual content goes in the text block beyond what the normal sanitizer already permits. Describe the tool to the model as **fallback evidence when text observation is insufficient or contradicts observed behavior** — never as a way to see the page by default. Per plan §12 item 2, capture is **agent-requested only** in this wave; automatic attachment on repeated failure is **deferred** and must have no code path here. ## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth / Consent (the dominant concern in this feature)**
  - Consent is an **explicit, stored, approved user grant** — `context.screenshots === true` in the effective `profile.yaml ⊕ index.db` view. Absent, unapproved, unset, malformed, and `false` are all denials, and they are deliberately indistinguishable to the model (the tool simply is not there).
  - Consent is **asymmetric to the existing precedent on purpose**. `context.location` defaults `true` (`!== false`) because it is behavior-preserving for a fact already being rendered. `context.screenshots` defaults `false` (`=== true`) because it is a new exposure of unmasked pixels. TASK-001 tests both lines so a future refactor cannot "unify" them.
  - Consent is **informed**: TASK-002 prints the raw-pixels / exposure / provider-transmission / local-retention warning **before** the write, in text and in `--json`, softened but never removed for a local provider.
  - Consent is **necessary but not sufficient**. Four further conditions gate registration (browser tools, model image input, no `--no-screenshots`, not zero-LLM), and two further gates guard each capture (the sensitive-screen latch, the capture budget).
  - Consent is **revocable** with `prefs set context.screenshots false` and `prefs --forget context.screenshots`; no dedicated revoke command is needed (plan §12 item 1). Revocation does not retroactively delete captures in past run directories, and the revocation message says so.
  - Consent is **overridable downward for one run** via the `--no-screenshots` negation, and never upward: there is no opt-in flag, so a run can only ever be _less_ capable than the saved profile says.
  - The existing per-tool **confirmation gateway** is untouched. A capture is not a mutating page action in the confirmation sense (the overlay is removed and nothing is submitted), so it does not enter the consent-gateway path; the grant _is_ its consent.
  - **Zero-LLM contexts have no consent surface at all**, by construction: scheduled/daemon runs and nested `workflow_run` are hard zero-LLM per memory, and there is no model to send a capture to. The tool is not registered there regardless of grant.

- **Error Handling**
  - Every gate **fails closed**. Denial paths: unavailable ⇒ not registered (no error code exists, because the tool cannot be called); latched ⇒ `SCREENSHOT_SENSITIVE_SCREEN` (`retryable: false` — it clears only on a real document-epoch change, so an immediate retry is a loop); budget ⇒ the existing `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` family naming which capture limit tripped; unresolvable ref ⇒ the existing `STALE_ELEMENT_REF`; capture/encoding failure ⇒ `SCREENSHOT_UNAVAILABLE`.
  - Per memory, **failure messages must say what actually happened**, carry what was observed and what recovery already ran, and give one cause-specific next step — and two failures sharing a code must not read identically. The latch failure explains that a secret may still be on screen and that capture resumes after the page navigates; the budget failure names the specific limit and the remaining allowance; they never share wording.
  - Per memory, **advice may only name a move the engine has an engineered path for**. No failure or hint may tell the model to "take a screenshot" in a catalog that does not export `browser_screenshot` (asserted in TASK-013).
  - Overlay handling uses `try/finally` with removal verification; an unverified removal is a **typed error**, never a silent success. A navigation race aborts the capture and discards the artifact rather than shipping a possibly-annotated or possibly-stale image.
  - Artifact validation in the middleware is a **fail-closed check on a pre-authorized artifact**: a missing file, sha mismatch, wrong mime, or oversize measurement drops the image and fails the call — it never "passes through anyway".
  - Errors are typed `Error` subclasses with safe, actionable context and are never silently swallowed (memory, Coding Standards).

- **Logging**
  - **The stable projection never carries pixels.** `tool-calls.jsonl` records only `{path, sha256, mime_type, width, height, bytes}`; `report.md` and ordinary Pino logs carry the same metadata only. The image-to-metadata swap happens **before** the normalized audit event crosses the provider seam, so there is no window in which the audit path holds base64.
  - **The raw Pi session log is capture-bearing by necessity** and is disclosed as such — by `yantra audit` (TASK-012) and by the grant warning (TASK-002), which names both provider transmission and local run-artifact retention. It is treated as a raw artifact, not a sanitized text log.
  - Pino logs at `info` record the _decision_ (capture accepted/denied, which gate, remaining budget) and never page content, never the accessible names of what was captured, and never secrets (memory, Logging).
  - **Captures are private files**: `runs/<id>/screenshots/` at `0o700`, files at `0o600` where the OS supports them, matching the existing `runs/<id>/captures/<ref>.txt` precedent. Paths are recorded run-relative so a moved run directory stays auditable.
  - **Encoding assertions must name their decoder.** Every test that reads an artifact to assert on encoding or on the absence of a byte signature reads it with an **explicit UTF-8 decoder** (plan §9); PowerShell 5.1's `Get-Content` defaults to ANSI and has produced false mojibake alarms twice. Byte signatures in tests are constructed from byte values and referred to in prose as the literal escape `\x89PNG` — never pasted as raw bytes into a source or spec file.
  - The run directory remains the durable observability artifact; this feature adds exactly one new sink (`screenshots/`) and no other (plan §10).

- **Architecture boundaries**
  - `packages/core` must never import `@yantra/agent`; the overlay and latch live in `packages/core/src/browser/`, and the tool that uses them lives in `packages/agent`.
  - Only `packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/` may import the provider SDK. `Model.input` is read in the adapter and crosses the seam as a plain boolean; Pi's `ImageContent` type is referenced only in `adapters/pi/tools/index.ts`'s mapping.
  - Explicit dependency injection throughout — the latch, capture writer, budget tracker, and availability flag are injected via `RunServices`, never reached through a module-level singleton.
  - **No website-specific logic anywhere** in this feature (memory): the capture, the overlay, and every gate work from generic structural signals only.
